access_status: full_text_hosted (CMO-Historical-Data-Monthly.xlsx + CMO-Pink-Sheet-September-2026.pdf committed; public-domain institutional data)
pipeline_mapping: FIRST anchor for the pipeline's commodity VALUE side — domains 1-5 all cover physics/cost, none touch market pricing. mineral_value_catalog.csv prices every tradable element (driving all of profitability_catalog.csv) from a static ref_price_usd_per_kg column cited only to 'USGS/LME/mineralogy reference' with NO registered source; this is the institutional primary behind that fallback. Parsed live: 71 commodity columns, monthly nominal USD 1960M01-2026M08 (updated 2026-09-02). Covers gold/platinum/silver/copper/nickel/aluminum/zinc/iron-ore; does NOT carry the minor PGMs Rh/Ir/Os/Ru/Pd (those stay on yfinance+USGS path). AUDIT FINDING: our ref column is a MIXED-DATED snapshot despite its uniform 2026-05-29 stamp — gold & nickel are current (match Apr-Jul 2026), but silver ($950/kg) matches no month since Jan 2024, copper last matched ~Jan 2025, platinum ~Jul 2025 => staleness correction candidates recorded in FINDINGS + extracted_data/r39_commodity_price_verification.csv. USGS Mineral Commodity Summary (the named fallback source) is bot-blocked from this machine (pubs.usgs.gov 403/404), so it is NOT registered here — recorded as attempted-but-unreachable.

short_title: LBMA (London Bullion Market Association) precious-metals fixings — daily benchmark prices for gold/silver/platinum/palladium in USD per troy ounce, 1968 to present; the institutional price authority that our code's "yfinance/LBMA path" actually resolves to
journal_or_series: LBMA official price data (prices.lbma.org.uk); JSON endpoints /json/{gold,silver,platinum,palladium}_am.json (+ _pm for Au/Pt/Pd), pulled live 2026-09-23; gold & silver series from 1968-01-02, Pt & Pd from 1990-04-02
access_status: open service — JSON pulled live this round (4 series; Au/Pt/Pd ~9.2k daily AM fixings 1990->, Ag ~14.85k since 1968); key numbers extracted to r45_lbma_precious_metals_key_numbers.csv
pipeline_mapping: SECOND anchor for the pipeline's commodity VALUE side — specifically the precious metals + minor PGMs that the worldbank_cmo_pink_sheet (R39) does NOT carry at daily resolution. This is the actual resolution of R39's open "yfinance/LBMA path": LBMA now registered and analyzable, not just cited. AUDIT vs our static ref_price_usd_per_kg (stamp 2026-05-29), compared at that SAME date (gap=0 trading days for all four): gold $150,000 ours vs LBMA $145,506 (+3.1%, fine); platinum $45,000 ours vs LBMA $61,472 (-26.8% LOW); palladium $48,000 ours vs LBMA $43,854 (+9.5%); silver $950 ours vs LBMA $2,436 (**-61% LOW**) => silver & platinum are stale-correction candidates (target repo is read-only so NOT applied here; recorded in FINDINGS + extracted_data). Basis: Au/Pt/Pd use the AM London fixing, Ag uses LBMA's single daily benchmark. Minor PGMs Rh/Ir/Os/Ru are still not carried by LBMA (stay on yfinance/USGS path).

pipeline_mapping: Closes R39/R45's open minor-PGM gap for 4 of 5 metals: the ONLY institutional source with published reference prices AND production statistics for Rh/Ir/Ru (LBMA carries none; USGS MCS bot-blocked). AUDIT vs our static ref_price_usd_per_kg + annual-production estimates, at JM Q1-2026 quotes (report covers through March 2026): rhodium $9,000/oz end-Dec-25 (~$289k/kg) vs ours $320k (+10.6% high); iridium ATH $8,000/oz Q1-26 (~$257k/kg) vs ours $160k (**ours -37.8% LOW**); ruthenium ATH $1,750/oz Q1-26 (~$56k/kg) vs ours $16k (**ours -71.6% LOW**; even -61.0% vs the more conservative end-of-25 record of $1,275/oz ≈ $41k/kg); platinum end-March $1,908/oz (~$61.3k/kg) corroborates R45's LBMA finding (ours -27% low). PRODUCTION: our estimates ~23 t Rh / 7.5 t Ir / 30 t Ru vs JM primary supply 2025 = 17.6 / 7.1 / 30.2 t -> Ir & Ru AGREE, **Rh ours +30.7% high (revision candidate)**. Osmium: NO published reference price in LBMA or JM and no production table => our $13k/kg row stays unanchored (recorded gap).
